written: 2026-10-31, before any C4 window ran (stage 1 and M1's ladder had run or were running; no window's code had run anywhere).
labels: inference unless marked; computed = arithmetic here from stage 1's 0.16 mm resistance and script A's declared values

design.windows: A0f with the moment tilted (register C4, reviews 1 and 2): the magnet fixed 150 mm above the tube's axis over s = 0, turning at 10 Hz (a kinematic motor on the world); FL-9 floored at s = 0 in the 1/4" tube, its moment of 1.68e-3 A m^2 tilted by alpha off the transverse plane towards the body's axis; the closed BEM at 0.16 mm (blob 0.5, margin 0.1 mm), Magnetic.Torque and Magnetic.Force, gravity, Contact.Projection; dt 0.5 ms (section 2 e). One window per alpha in {4, 2, 6} deg and per direction (6 windows), each 0.1 s of transient and 5 turns (1,200 steps).
design.checks: at every step, each with a stop (as A0f's pass, section 5): the drag's resistance positive definite and finite, every wall read accepted; and a stop if the body's displacement along the pass over its last turn is not positive. Run in chunks of 20 steps, every step of a chunk checked, the window stopped at the first failing step and saved after every chunk (a window cut by the timeout is rerun from its start).
design.metric: for a complete window: the speed along the pass over its 5 turns and the body's cone angle (its axis's angle from the tube's, per turn); per alpha, the two-direction mean speed. The control: the planted alpha = 4 deg recovered in the cone angle within 20% or the turns' scatter, whichever is larger (review 2, N22).

C4-P1.predicted: every window (alpha 2, 4 and 6 deg, both directions) stops at its every-step check before its first turn completes (50 ms)
C4-P1.basis: computed: the transverse turning resistance times omega against m|B| is 0.24 to 0.49 (about y) and 0.14 to 0.27 (about z), so a free body's axis follows the tilted moment onto a cone of nearly alpha; at alpha = 2 deg the tilt rate is about 6.6 rad/s (7 to 8 steps to 1.4 deg). The contact holds the centre's offset, not the ends (7j-a: the lateral surface's NaN at a 0.042 rad tilt, MIME-ANO-121): the end crest sits at 0.9685 R and leaves the table's readable range (0.997 R) at a tilt of 1.39 deg; half the 0.1 mm gap (0.77 deg) may make the resistance indefinite first (7j-a: indefinite at gap/spacing 0.29).

C4-P2.predicted: by the definiteness check or the wall check, at a tilt between 0.5 and 1.6 deg, within the first 80 steps (40 ms), earliest for 6 deg

C4-P3.predicted: neither the two-direction mean speed nor the cone angle can be read for any alpha, and the planted-alpha control cannot run (so it is not a pass); C4's dev1 bound stays open

C4-P4.what: if a window does complete (against C4-P1)
C4-P4.predicted: its cone angle between 0.5 alpha and alpha, and its two-direction mean speed within 2% of A0f's frictionless reading at s = 0 (second order in alpha)
C4-P4.basis: the register's prediction (second order while floored)

C4-P5.predicted: under $1.5 if C4-P1 holds (six builds and compilations, under 100 steps each); at most $8.3 if no window stops (7,200 steps at about 1 s, six compilations, x1.4)
C4-P5.basis: stage 1: 0.90 s per node step at 0.16 mm (computed)

framework_meaning_if_P1_holds: a finding for the maintainer, not on the register's list: C4's test needs a contact that restrains the body's ends (or its orientation), which dev1's projection contact does not have; the same limit stops A0f's pass wherever the body tilts by about 1.4 deg.
